title: T1589.003 — Gather Victim Identity Information - Employee Names
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Gather Victim Identity Information - Employee Names with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated simulation: Employee-name reconnaissance against a fictional company. It shows each step of the technique and what defenders can see. A written version of every step is in the story below the canvas. Use the step buttons under the canvas, or focus the canvas and press the left and right arrow keys.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: Builds the name list, the org chart, and later the fake persona. Everything in the early steps happens outside your systems.

nodes.label: Public web
nodes.tip: Your team, leadership, and careers pages. Names, photos, and titles here are the raw material of the whole campaign.

nodes.label: Professional networks
nodes.tip: Public profiles, speaker lists, and conference pages. They add roles, projects, and reporting lines to bare names.

nodes.label: Leak forum
nodes.tip: Old breach dumps pair staff names with working email addresses and confirm your address format.

nodes.label: Mail gateway
nodes.tip: Your mail edge. The first corporate telemetry the campaign touches when persona-based lures arrive.

nodes.label: Employees
nodes.tip: People whose names were collected. Finance, IT, the helpdesk, and executives are the usual priorities.

nodes.label: SOC
nodes.tip: Your detection and response team. They act on reports, feed matches, and web-log bursts.

nodes.label: Intel feeds
nodes.tip: Leak monitoring and brand watching. They can reveal the list and the fake support brand before the lures land.

steps.title: Pick the target
steps.caption: The attacker chooses Aurelia Pay, a fast-growing payments company, and opens a worksheet with one column: people. No company system has been touched.
steps.defender: Nothing to see yet. Target selection happens entirely outside your visibility.

steps.title: Build the persona
steps.caption: The attacker creates an IT service desk identity: a lookalike address, a real manager's name, and a story about a routine account check. Every detail in it is true.
steps.defender: Real names are what make the persona strong. Expect calls and messages that quote your own staff.

steps.title: An employee reports the lure
steps.caption: A finance employee notices the message quotes a colleague who left last year, and presses the report button. The report shows which names the attacker used.
steps.defender: Reports are your best signal. Make the button easy to find and triage within the hour.

steps.title: Intel confirms, defenders respond
steps.caption: The leak feed confirms staff names in a fresh dump. The SOC blocks the sender and the lookalike domain, briefs the named staff, and files tickets to thin the public pages.
steps.defender: Recon cannot be undone, but the attacks that depend on it can be blunted. Record everything for trend analysis.
